subject: PrivSec handoff: data residency & break-glass scoping for Riverrun
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Lane <sofia.lane@riverrun.finance>, Paul Chen <paul.chen@riverrun.finance>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 15:04:00 +0000
Subject: PrivSec handoff: data residency & break-glass scoping for Riverrun

Hi Sofia / Paul — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can loop in Eng/PrivSec and get you a draft DPA/redlines.

Recap (from our discovery):
- Data types: transaction metadata and user profile fields; PII fields confirmed: full name, email, partial SSN-like identifier (last 4), billing address.
- Retention: you said default session logs 30 days, billing and audit 90 days; some analytics cached up to 12 months.
- Residency: production must live in EU regions; non-prod can be US.
- Support access: on-call devs need scoped access for troubleshooting; you'd like just-in-time (JIT) break-glass with approval + audit trail.
- Logging & evidence: you asked for audit logs for all support sessions, redacted sample logs, and SOC 2 evidence.

Next steps I propose (please confirm / correct):
1) Sofia: confirm the exact retention windows (by data class) and whether backups must be EU-only.
2) Riverrun legal: we’ll circulate a draft DPA with the standard Redwood clauses + proposed JIT break-glass language; please flag any must-have edits.
3) Internal (Marissa/Ben): scope the implementation options for RBAC, ephemeral support access, and logging formats; can you produce a short ops checklist + artifacts we can share by Fri 2026-08-07?
4) I’ll book a 30-min follow-up for Aug 6 to review the draft DPA and technical scoping.

Attachments: PII-data-mapping.xlsx (spreadsheet stub) — please review.

Thanks — Karthik
--
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Lane <sofia.lane@riverrun.finance>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paul Chen <paul.chen@riverrun.finance>, legal@riverrun.finance
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 18:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: PrivSec handoff: data residency & break-glass scoping for Riverrun

Hi Karthik — thanks for the clear notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- Retention by class (confirm): PII contact info (name, email) = 180 days; partial identifier (last4) = 90 days; billing records (transactional) = 7 years (regulatory); analytics/aggregates = 12 months. Backups containing PII must be EU-resident for production.
- Residency: EU only for production datastore and backups; staging can be US.
- Support access: we require JIT break-glass that integrates with Okta/SCIM, approval chain (manager or security on-call), and a signed attest/audit exported per session.
- Logging: we need immutable audit trails (WORM preferred) for admin actions for at least 1 year, and deltas for data access events for 90 days.

Sofia
Security lead — Riverrun Finance
sofia.lane@riverrun.finance

Forwarding Riverrun answers (below). Marissa / Ben — can you own an ops/engineering response? Specifically we need:

A) Short doc (1-2 pages) that maps: data classes -> retention policy -> storage residency (prod/backups), and clearly states what we can guarantee.
B) RBAC role matrix proposal: admin / support / auditor / read-only operator and the minimum privileges for each role (both console and API).
C) Support access design: two options with pros/cons:
   1) Ephemeral role via Okta with time-limited session + approval flow (recommended).
   2) Scoped long-lived support tokens + IP restrictions (fall-back).
   Include required telemetry (session start/stop, commands executed, file accesses) and how we export audit logs (S3 bucket link pattern / JSON schema).
D) Evidence list: SOC 2 cert (if we can share), sample audit log (redacted), and a proposed DPA redline.

Timeline: can you deliver the doc + artifacts by 2026-08-07 EOD? Riverrun needs this to finish internal risk review. If timeline is tight, flag which items need more time.

Thanks — Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 09:13:00 +0000

Thanks — I can take point and will draft the ops rollup. Quick notes from Eng perspective: 

- Data residency: we can guarantee EU-only production in our EU region (db + backups) using customer-specified region tags; need to confirm whether Riverrun requires encrypted backups with a customer-managed key (CMK) — if yes, we need their KMS ARN and timeline.
- Retention: we can set per-table retention windows; billing (7yrs) will be archived to an EU-compliant cold storage tier (costs TBD).
- RBAC mapping: propose three roles for support: Support-Triage (read-only logs + limited debug ops), Support-Session (ephemeral elevation for a defined time window), and Support-Audit (view-only, no modify). Admin role kept to Riverrun SREs.
- Break-glass: recommend Okta-based JIT using SCIM + ephemeral AWS STS tokens issued after approval; sessions will be recorded and a .json audit bundle exported to an encrypted S3 bucket (WORM option via object lock).
- Evidence: we can attach (1) SOC2 attestation (PDF stub), (2) sample redacted audit log (json stub), (3) suggested DPA redlines (redlines_DPA_v1.pdf).

I should be able to assemble the 1-2 page ops matrix + artifacts by Thu 2026-08-06 EOD. Ben — can you add a short schema for audit logs (fields we will include) and confirm the export path?

—Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
